Apple is set to report its fiscal third-quarter results for the period ending June today, followed by the usual analyst Q&A. The company's market cap briefly crossed $5 trillion before easing back slightly.

Today will be Tim Cook's last earnings call as CEO, and analysts aren't expecting any surprises—but there is one very big question…

No surprises expected

Apple already said back in April that it expects year-over-year revenue growth of between 14% and 17%, and Zacks reports that the consensus estimate sits almost exactly in the middle of that range.

While that earns it a Zacks Rank of Hold rather than Buy, the firm also noted that Apple has beaten consensus estimates in each of the past four quarters.

Motley Fool's latest aggregated rating gives it a Buy, but notes the average price target is essentially flat. The site says this isn't unusual, given that analysts' price targets typically lag when a stock has shot up quickly over a relatively short period.

But one big question

Investors will be paying very close attention to Apple's outlook on the impact of its new Apple Upgrade program.

The company is, of course, hoping that letting consumers spread the cost of products over monthly installments will offset the impact of recent price increases, but is Apple expecting the program to simply win back sales it would otherwise have lost, or is it expecting it to drive significant growth?

That will be the key question driving how the market reacts to today's results.
